§10.4.3 Checklists

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

forms-checklists · forms checkboxes

✅ Normative

Each checklist item MUST be rendered box-first — the box before its printed label — and items MUST be nested under their group label. A group-level box MUST stay on its group's line. A form's group labels MUST NOT be promoted to document headings.

A list of items each led by a box, sometimes under a group label that carries a box of its own. Nothing is being answered; the page is a to-do list or a required-documents list.

☐ Division 9 rate filings
    ☐ Transmittal information
    ☐ Certification (EC-1, residential property)
    ☐ Rate filing checklist (Exhibit A)

- [ ] **Division 9 rate filings**
  - [ ] Transmittal information
  - [ ] Certification (EC-1, residential property)
  - [ ] Rate filing checklist (Exhibit A)

A checklist item has no caption above it and no label before its box, so neither shape of The Key-Value List§10.3.2 applies unchanged: it is not an option of a captioned group, and it is not a labelled field with a box in the value position. It is rendered box-first, like an option line.

✅ Sample — a filing checklist

Two bold group labels, each with a large box before it; ten and one indented items under them, each with a smaller box. Four labelled fill-ins sit in the top-right corner.

Blank lines used as check marks

A short printed line that stands where a box would be, in front of a checklist item, is a checklist control: it MUST be rendered [ ] (or [x] when marked). [blank] MUST be used only when the line asks for a written value.

✅ Sample — blank lines used as check marks

Every item is led by ___ rather than a box, including the indented * SCHEDULE A … * SCHEDULE J run. A REFERENCE column of citations sits at the right margin under its own printed header, aligned to the items, so each section is a two-column table whose item cells hold the checklist.

A grid of checklists

A ruled grid whose cells each hold a checklist is a table: the cells are the table's content, and each cell's checklist is rendered as list items inside the cell.

✅ Sample — nine checklists in a grid

A three-by-three ruled grid, each cell a centred title over a list of boxed items, some with an italic qualifier. The cells are the table's content and the boxes are the cells' content.

A box printed before an id

The order of box and id. A lettered or numbered item can print its box before its id: ☐ (h) The crime of …. It MUST be rendered box first, then the escaped id — - [ ] \[h\] The crime of … — so that the box always opens the line whether or not an id follows it.

✅ Sample — a box before a lettered id

Items (h) to (k) each print a box, then the letter id, then a paragraph with blanks inside it. Each line opens with the box, then the escaped id: - [ ] \[h\].
